question: How do I operate the amux service (board, projects, workers, schedules, memory, diagnostics) from any agent session over its HTTP API?
decision: which API family matches the request (board vs projects vs workers vs schedules vs memories vs diagnostics)
whether a write operation must be confirmed with the user before it is executed
how to handle a 401, 404, or gate-blocked 409 response
evidence: HTTP status code and JSON body returned by the amux API
card id and status echoed back by the board API
success_measure: The requested operation completes with a 2xx response and its result is visible in the amux dashboard (for example the card exists with the intended status).
outcome: Any agent session can operate the amux service over its HTTP API without repo-specific knowledge.
use_cases: create, claim, and advance board cards
create a project and submit an outcome that the server decomposes into project tasks
read and write session or global memory

examples.description: Create a board card through the /amux-skill skill

examples.invocation: /amux-skill projects create my-project "build the import page"
examples.description: Create an amux project and submit its first outcome
List amux workers with their current status

documentation_sources: GET /api/debug/routes on the running server (live route table, wins over any written doc)
the API map documented in SKILL.md
references/long-tail.md in this skill directory (per-route examples for the long-tail families)
required_capabilities: network reachability to the amux host on port 8824
readiness_checks: GET /api/board with Authorization: Bearer returns HTTP 200

approval_required: confirm with the user before write calls: create/update/delete board cards, create or reconfigure projects, send messages to workers, trigger schedules

authoritative_sources: amux HTTP API, verified against GET /api/debug/routes on the live server
relationships: a card optionally names the session/worker that owns it
a project task carries project_group naming the project it belongs to
a schedule targets exactly one session
a memory is scoped global, group, or worker
field_semantics: status is backlog/todo/doing/done plus custom columns; verified is a separate gate from done
gate is a list of criteria derived from the card type
source_ref is the evidence pointer required for done
invariants: card ids increase monotonically and are never reused
non-todo status transitions are gated by type-derived criteria
freshness_and_pagination: board, workers and schedules reads are full-snapshot responses (no pagination on the routes documented here)
diagnostic endpoints take a since_h window
nullability: optional fields such as desc, session, end, location may be absent; treat missing as unset, not as an error
readiness_checks: GET /api/debug/routes lists every route family this skill uses

should_trigger: add a task to the amux board
create an amux project and submit its first goal
